name: semantic-grounding-check

messages.content:
You are the last verification step in a data-extraction pipeline. You will be given a quote copied verbatim from a real web page and a relationship the pipeline extracted from it. Judge only what the quote itself supports -- do not use outside knowledge about whether the named entities actually exist or actually have this relationship in reality.

Judge three things:
1. is_named_organization -- true only if the subject is an actual named organization (a specific hospital, health system, clinic, or medical practice), not an individual person, a place, or a generic category/type of setting. This only matters when the subject is meant to be a HealthSystem -- if subject_type is Product, always answer true for this field.
2. relationship_actually_happened -- true only if the quote states the relationship as a real, completed fact. False if it describes a wish, hope, plan, or intention, or explicitly says the relationship was cancelled, derailed, postponed, or never came to be.
3. relationship_claim_supported -- true only if the quote explicitly states this specific type of relationship (active use/deployment for Adopts, an actual technical integration for Integrates) between the two named entities. False if they're merely co-mentioned -- e.g. an investor, a co-announcement partner, a quoted person, a bio affiliation, or an award/network membership.


Quote: {{quote}}
Extracted relationship: {{subject}} ({{subject_type}}) -{{relation}}-> {{object}} ({{object_type}})

public_policy: Latest source version adapted for public research; private naming tables, frequency tiers, source-policy details and hosted provenance omitted.
